GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: Revision 2026-10-23 (evening): this bundle's architecture flipped after a four-way live bake-off, and its scope absorbed the tab-context-menu export feature on the owner's instruction. The original draft (same morning) planned a JSON document-tree payload written by a new Rust module (docx-rs + hand-rolled RTF). Three things killed that plan. First, evidence: the bake-off ran markdown-docx, remark-docx, mdast2docx and docx's own docx/html importer on a shared EN+RU fixture (research/2026-10-23-docx-bakeoff/), and the docx/html arm — fed exactly the kind of HTML Mark's styled-HTML export already produces — won or tied every contested construct: KaTeX output became native OMML equations (content-verified: m:f, m:nary, m:rad with readable math text), markdown-style footnotes became real Word footnotes, task checkboxes became native w14 checkboxes with state, a display formula inside a numbered list stayed un-numbered while every markdown re-parser let it consume a list number (the exact shape of upstream bug reports), and front matter needs only an explicit pre-pass strip — muya renders it as a pre block we control — whereas all three markdown re-parsers leaked the raw YAML as literal body text (verified in the bake-off; the R-3c strip is pinned by test). Second, reuse: the heavy pre-pass machinery landed since the morning draft — M-065's embedLocalImages util exists in code and already runs on the styledHtml branch, so the DOCX path composes existing machines instead of building a parallel muya serializer. Third, footprint: the whole arm lazy-loads at ~237 KB gzip (measured), zero Rust code, zero new commands — the size-first pitch survives a new export format untouched. RTF left the bundle because the same survey found no living ready-made RTF writer in any ecosystem we touch (npm dead or hollow, Rust niche, the native macOS endpoint lossy on import); deferring beats hand-rolling "just in case". The tab-menu merge is a scope decision, not an afterthought: the owner asked for export entry points at the file itself, and the backlog item ("export actions next to Copy path") is exactly that feature — one behavior, two doors, one bundle.

Alternatives.Alternative: Rust-side writer module (m066_office_export.rs: docx-rs DOCX + hand-rolled RTF over a JSON document-tree payload) — the superseded primary, kept as the named fallback. What it would buy: RTF in the same module later, zero renderer weight. What the bake-off priced: a parallel muya serializer to build and keep true, our own math/footnote/checkbox stories (the two hard tails the winner gets for free), and a hand-rolled RTF writer against no demonstrated demand. It becomes the primary again if the importer fails on production-CSS documents at implementation start (spec Assumptions name the flip).

markdown-docx (vace, v1.7.1) — the bake-off's close second: marked-15 lineage (muya's parser family), real footnotes, KaTeX→MathML→OMML math, native checkboxes, clean imageAdapter API. Costs: front-matter strip pre-pass mandatory (leaks as text, verified), display math inside a numbered list consumes a list number (matches its open issue #30), and a second katex copy (^0.16 vs our ^0.18, ~70-80 KB gzip in the lazy chunk) unless aliased. It is the engine named in the spec's fallback flip.

remark-docx (inokawa, 0.3.29) — eliminated on fixture evidence: task checkboxes dropped entirely, code blocks and inline code unstyled without its shiki plugin, docx pinned at exactly 9.7.1. Its strengths (RTL, two-column layouts, plugin system) do not offset those gaps for v1.

@m2d/mdast2docx monorepo — lightest bundle (223 KB) and direct LaTeX-AST→OpenXML math, but no footnotes exist anywhere in its ecosystem (npm 404 on a footnote package; issue tracker holds only release PRs), and it leaked front matter twice. Out until footnotes exist.
pandoc-wasm (official, pandoc org) — closed with numbers: 58.6 MB unpacked, GPL-2.0-or-later (incompatible with MAS distribution), no PDF output. Not revisited.

Native macOS endpoint (NSAttributedString reads HTML, writes .rtf/.docx/.odt in-process) — lossy legacy-HTML import, main-thread, TextEdit-grade fidelity, math does not survive; documented as RTF Plan B for the deferred RTF decision, not a DOCX contender.

DeferredDecisions.Decision: RTF export — deferred until field demand (legal/medical legacy workflows). Plan A: hand-rolled Rust writer (realistic budget 1-2k lines with tables, list templates, hex images). Plan B: the native NSAttributedString endpoint accepting legacy-import fidelity. Both documented in the 2026-10-23 survey.
A Word TOC field in the output (prompts "update fields" on open) — revisit after owner reaction; getTOC() already provides the data.

Per-format export settings UI — DECIDED 2026-10-23: Word ships modal-less (no dialog at all, remembered geometry, print-path precedent); the "quick export" open option from the tab-menu item is absorbed (quick export simply IS the export); the Export settings section for all formats stays in the backlog rework ("Export without the settings modal"), unblocked by nothing and blocked by nothing.

Engine flip trigger — if docx/html fails the plan-time re-run on production-CSS muya HTML, the fallback flip to markdown-docx is pre-authorized by the spec's assumption wording; anything beyond that returns to the owner.
Follow-up comment to dolanmiu/docx discussion #3827 at release time — drafted with the change, sent only with owner approval (standing rule).

Scenarios.Scenario: An agent drafts a spec in Mark; the owner hits File → Export to Word… and the save dialog is the first and only UI (no settings modal); they send report.docx to a manager, who opens a document with real headings, a real table, working hyperlinks, editable native equations and real footnotes — no pandoc, nothing to install, nothing to explain. When the notification rework lands, the success card quietly offers "Export settings" for the rare wrong-geometry day.

The owner right-clicks a background tab with unsaved edits, picks Export to Word… from the menu that already holds Copy path; the tab activates, the current buffer (edits included) converts, the save dialog offers the file's basename.docx — the same flow as the File menu, one door closer.

An App Store user on a sandboxed Mac exports a Cyrillic-heavy study note with inline math and a pele diagram: the equations arrive as editable Word equations, the diagram as a crisp 2x PNG, the one 40 MB TIFF the document references produces a "9 of 10 images embedded" notice instead of a failure, and no network request leaves the app (CSP forbids it; the design agrees).

C-1.Name: Heading ladder H1-H6 over Cyrillic text
C-1.Expected: Unzipped output: six paragraphs with w:pStyle Heading1..Heading6 (via styleMap), outline levels intact, UTF-8 Cyrillic verbatim; both fixtures open in Word/Pages/LibreOffice with a working navigation pane.

C-2.Name: Inline emphasis cluster: bold + italic + strike + inline code + link on one paragraph
C-2.Expected: Separate runs with the right properties; the link is a w:hyperlink whose Id resolves in document.xml.rels to the original URL; inline code carries a monospace font (bake-off: Courier run from the docx/html importer). No run leaks a property to its neighbors. The sibling fenced-code fixture (Prism token spans from muya's renderHtml highlight) renders monospace with token-level color recorded as an explicit per-construct checklist verdict, not a promise.

C-3.Name: Task list with mixed states and nesting under an ordered parent
C-3.Expected: w14:checkbox elements whose w14:checked values equal the muya states (bake-off: 0/1 carry verified); list levels carry the nesting; states come from the rendered HTML, never a markdown re-parse.

C-4.Name: Ragged table with per-column alignment (left/center/right) and CJK cell text
C-4.Expected: A single w:tbl with per-column w:jc matching the muya meta (bake-off: center/right verified); CJK text verbatim; no dropped cells.

C-5.Name: Local PNG referenced three times (1.2 MiB) plus one inline data: URL image
C-5.Expected: One read for the thrice-referenced file (M-065 dedup), PNG bytes embedded as docx media parts, three placements; the data: URL image lands without a disk read; notice counters report 0 skipped, 2 embedded.

C-6.Name: Image corners: 40 MiB local file, deleted local file, remote https image
C-6.Expected: All three skip the embed pass (8 MiB cap / read failure / no-network rule), the document stays intact, the remote one degrades to alt text plus URL, the notice reports "0 of 3" per the localized copy; export succeeds and the file is written.

C-7.Name: pele diagram with theme variables in one document
C-7.Expected: The figure block is replaced by a rasterized 2x PNG img data-URL in document order before conversion (C-56 machinery), and lands in the output as embedded media at its tree position; the unit test pins document-order correlation.

C-8.Name: Math: display block and inline $…$ with LaTeX, including a formula inside a numbered list
C-8.Expected: Native OMML equations with real structure (fraction and n-ary content asserted); the display formula inside the numbered list does NOT carry list numbering (renders 1, 2 — bake-off-pinned against the 1, 2 (formula), 3 failure of the re-parser arms).

C-9.Name: Footnote reference mid-paragraph with RU definition containing bold
C-9.Expected: Real Word footnotes: footnoteReference ids resolve into footnotes.xml whose entries carry the Cyrillic text with its bold run (bake-off verified on the remark-rehype shape). Muya emits its own shape (a.footnote-ref[role=doc-noteref], section.footnotes[role=doc-endnotes] with li#fn…[role=doc-endnote]) — the pre-pass reshapes it data-only to the recognized shape, and the unit test pins both muya's real markup and the resulting footnotes.xml. Footnotes are ON by default in Mark (preferences footnote: true), so this is the default path, not an option.

C-10.Name: Front matter document (--- title … ---)
C-10.Expected: No front-matter text in the output: the pre-pass strips muya's pre.front-matter block (muya's renderer emits front matter as a pre block — verified renderer.js:13; without the strip it would land as a code block). The strip is pinned on muya's real export output in the unit matrix.

C-11.Name: Hostile text: raw braces, control bytes, fake footnote markup, fake style attributes
C-11.Expected: Round-trips into a valid .docx whose concatenated text nodes equal the source text; the DOM-parsed conversion plus docx serialization escaping means none of it becomes document structure.

C-12.Name: Cancel, tab-menu gating, and the PDF/print/HTML regression boundary
C-12.Expected: Cancel invokes mt_fs_write_binary zero times, writes nothing, shows no notice. Untitled tabs show the export group disabled exactly like Copy path; a background-tab export activates the tab first. The pdf/print/styledHtml branches are untouched (editor.vue diff shows no shared-line changes beyond the dispatch regex); print-export.spec.ts and export-html-images.spec.ts pass unmodified; mt_export_pdf / mt_print_webview are never invoked from the docx branch (pinned).

C-13.Name: Lazy chunk and startup cost
C-13.Expected: The entry chunk contains no docx code (CI guard on the built output); the docx dynamic chunk ≤ 300 KB gzip (237 KB measured in the bake-off harness); first-export click pays one dynamic import; a second export in the same session pays none.

C-14.Name: Modal-less flow and the notification degradation/upgrade path
C-14.Expected: No exportSettings component mounts on the docx path (e2e-pinned); the save dialog is the first and only UI, pre-filled filename.md → filename.docx; geometry equals the remembered last-used options (print-path storage). The success call passes the quiet "Export settings" actions descriptor with source 'export'; today's legacy wrapper drops it silently (no error, no UI); under C-NOTIFICATION-SYSTEM the SAME call renders the quiet action with zero export-side changes — the upgrade is automatic, pinned as a corner in that bundle.

Revision.note: Evening revision per the 2026-10-23 bake-off (rounds 1-3 + post-audit) and the owner's instruction to merge the tab-context-menu export feature. Primary flipped from the Rust writer (m066, docx-rs + hand-rolled RTF) to the renderer-side docx/html arm; RTF moved out of v1; tab-menu export group merged in; math/footnote/checkbox coverage upgraded from documented degradations to bake-off-verified native constructs. The two clean review passes below were performed on the SUPERSEDED draft and do not transfer; fresh correctness/security/UX/performance passes against this revision are required before owner approval.

Correctness.Note: Applied to the morning draft (Rust writer): semantic source is the muya block tree; figure machinery reuse; no webview on the path. Retained where still true for the revision: no-webview/no-Objective-C argument, M-065 cap semantics, C-56 reuse, document-order correlation. Superseded items: JSON payload, docx-rs, RTF writer, blocksToDocumentTree, mt_export_document command.

Security.Note: Retained for the revision: no new capabilities; save-dialog path validation; no network at export; hostile-text round-trip (now via DOM parsing + docx serialization instead of RTF escaping); notices carry counts only. UX.Note: Retained: flat menu item beside PDF/HTML, PDF-branch save flow, silent geometry reuse, native-copy localization, named Word styles. New in the revision awaiting fresh pass: the tab-menu group semantics (activate-then-export, pathname gating, label parity).

Review.Findings: Pass A (correctness and GRACE contracts) and pass B (security, verification, UX) each returned findings; all were fixed in the morning draft before this verdict. Verified facts that remain load-bearing for the revision: no user-facing pandoc export exists today (menu grep + shim probe only); MAS hard-disables the bridge (m015 cfg); mt_fs_write_binary exists (m013b fs.rs:370); DF-007's branch summary extends naturally; e2e helper/shim names and the three regression specs exist as cited; strict GRACE anchor conventions followed. Correctness.Note: Every code citation re-verified against the tree; three findings fixed in the spec. (1) "Zero grammar drift by construction" was overstated: the styled export HTML is a re-parse through muya's OWN marked fork (exportHtml.renderHtml: footnote / superSub options, Prism highlight, KaTeX renderer) — same grammar family as the editor, not a third-party dialect, but a re-parse; R-3a/R-4 reworded to the accurate claim. (2) Front matter DOES appear in the export HTML — muya's renderer emits it as a pre.front-matter block (renderer.js:13, verified); the "cannot leak" claim was false and is replaced by an explicit strip step in the R-3c pre-pass (the morning draft's metadata-not-body stance, now deliberate), pinned by test. (3) Muya's footnote shape is class/role-based (a.footnote-ref[role=doc-noteref], section.footnotes[role=doc-endnotes]) and differs from the bake-off's remark-rehype shape; R-5 now names both shapes and the data-only adaptation; footnotes are ON by default (preferences.js:222 true vs muya default false). Verified as cited: m009 export items + command pattern (exportPdf/exportHtml at ~567); handleExport regex /^pdf|print|styledHtml$/ at editor.vue:1816; exportStyledHTML + embedLocalImages(rawHtml, documentDir) composition with counts; EMBED_CAP_BYTES 8 MiB; mt_fs_write_binary at m013b fs.rs:370 with m010 validation and C-24 grants; tab-menu items carry enabled: !!pathname and handlers receive tab.id; M-066 free in the graph; DF-007 ExportHtmlOrPdf exists; m015_pandoc.rs:32 is mt_pandoc_status. Performance.Note: Cost model per export click: one muya re-render (already paid by any HTML export), the M-065 embed pass (bounded reads, 8 MiB cap), one htmlToContent DOM walk, Packer serialization, one binary IPC write — the 3-second budget on the 100 KB stress fixture stands, and the checklist now also runs the CJK-heavy real-world sample (27 KB, ~4400 CJK chars, 330 math spans — the crash fixture) so math-heavy conversion time is measured, not assumed.
